After a two-year update gap, Apple is developing a new iMac with the M6 chip and will refresh its colour options, expected to launch "by the end of the year," according to Bloomberg journalist Mark Gurman.

The iMac doesn't get updated often — it previously skipped the M2 and M5 chip generations and still doesn't offer a larger screen size option, with Apple instead directing high-end users to the Mac Studio or Mac mini paired with a Studio Display. Despite this, Apple is still preparing to release a new version with the M6 chip.

Gurman notes that this update will bring "some new colour options," though he didn't mention specifics. Apple tweaked the colours slightly with the 2024 M4 version, but the actual 7 colour options remained the same, with only minor tonal differences. The new iMac is also expected to launch by the end of the year:

This means autumn will be quite significant for the Mac. A redesigned MacBook Pro will feature a touchscreen and Tandem OLED, a new base 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip, a new Mac Studio with M5 Max and M5 Ultra (depending on supply), and a new iMac with the M6 chip. Another possibility is a new Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro, though that product is expected to launch later.

Apple's M6 chip will be the first Mac chip built on the new 2nm process, but reportedly there will be no M6 Pro, M6 Max, or M6 Ultra versions — Apple will instead accelerate the launch of the M7 series chips.
